MobAI-App/simslim.description: Run more iOS simulators on one Mac by disabling background daemons a simulator doesn't need
MobAI-App/simslim.readme:
# simslim

Run a lot more iOS, Apple TV (tvOS), Apple Watch (watchOS), and Apple Vision Pro (visionOS) simulators on one Mac by turning off the background daemons a simulator doesn't need.

A freshly booted iOS simulator starts around 180 background services: Siri, Spotlight indexing, photo analysis, News, wallpaper posters, iCloud sync, and so on. None of it matters when you're using the simulator for development, testing, or CI. simslim switches those services off, which cuts each simulator's memory roughly 4x. On the same laptop you go from a handful of simulators to a screenful.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4665e41-43b4-49cd-9388-3da533e9fd7b

*12 slim simulators on a 16 GB M1 Pro, each driven by its own Claude Code agent through MobAI. Stock simulators start thrashing at around 5.*

## Numbers

One simulator, booted stock and then slimmed, same device and settle time (M1 Pro, 16 GB):

| | Stock | Slim |
|---|---|---|
| Processes | 258 | 70 |
| Memory | 4.0 GB | 0.9 GB |

Memory here is phys_footprint, the figure Activity Monitor shows, which counts compressed and swapped pages. That's what decides how many simulators fit before the machine starts swapping. Run `simslim measure <udid>` to see it for any booted simulator.

`status` and `measure` answer different questions. `status` counts only the
allowlisted launchd labels SimSlim manages; it is not a live-process count. A
slim boot still runs required core services plus system apps and extensions.
`measure` walks every process under that simulator's `launchd_sim` and sums
`phys_footprint`. A sum of `ps` RSS values is not comparable because RSS counts
shared mappings once for every process that maps them.

## Install

```sh
brew install mobai-app/tap/simslim
```

or

```sh
go install github.com/mobai-app/simslim/cmd/simslim@latest
```

macOS only, and you need Xcode with an iOS, tvOS, watchOS, or visionOS Simulator
runtime, since simslim drives simulators through `xcrun simctl`.

All four platforms use the same commands and service profiles. `list`, `top`,
and the macOS app show each device's platform; JSON device records include
`platform` (`iOS`, `tvOS`, `watchOS`, or `visionOS`) alongside the numeric
`osVersion`. The existing memory figures and category estimates were measured on
iOS; savings on Apple TV, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro depend on their
runtime and workload.
The profile is an allowlist of disable overrides, so labels absent from a
particular runtime do not represent

Once installed, you own the code; modify it freely. - **Visual memorability** — Rare but practical components: the Dither Pop halftone series, an optical magnifier, ASCII backgrounds, multi-curtain preloaders — not another set of basic controls. - **Motion first** — Tactile interactions, inertial drag and sequenced animation. Motion / GSAP / Three.js are introduced per component and declared explicitly. - **Zero runtime lock-in** — No dependency on shadcn/ui or TanStack Start. rinkitadhana/openside.readme:
### OPENSIDE **Openside** is an open-source, self-hostable recording studio - capture high-quality meetings, podcasts, and screen recordings with multi-track, per-participant recording, then finalize them into clean, downloadable video. [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Self-hostable](https://img.shields.io/badge/self--hostable-yes-brightgreen.svg)](#getting-started-local-dev) [![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-orange.svg)](#contributing) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-100%25-3178c6.svg)
--- ## Features - **Studio-quality recording** - crisp video up to 4K with clear, high-quality audio - **Multi-track, per-participant output** - each speaker on their own track, ready to edit - **Screen recorder** - standalone screen + camera capture with pause/resume, codec fallback, and the camera composited in a single encode - **Crash-safe uploads** - recordings stream up in chunks while you record, with live per-participant upload progress and automatic recovery of stuck takes - **Projects & library** - every meeting and screen take in one place, with server-side search from the command menu - **Comments & descriptions** - threaded comments with replies and edits on every recording, plus a description per project - **Calendar & scheduling** - schedule meetings, send calendar invites, and see past recordings and screen takes on a calendar - **Shareable recordings** - share any recording from your projects with a link - **Export in any format** - download your recordings as MP4, WebM, MP3, or WAV - **Cheaper than SaaS** - no per-seat fees, pay only for the infra you use - **Use it for free** - connect your own LiveKit and storage in settings to unlock unlimited, watermark-free recording at no cost beyond your own usage - **Open source & self-hostable** - MIT licensed, no vendor lock-in - **Editor** - coming soon --- ## Architecture Openside is **two apps**: a frontend (`web`) and a backend (`core`). `core` builds once and runs as several processes - the API and the media workers. ```mermaid flowchart LR W[Browser · web app] -->|REST + WebSocket| API[core · Express API] W <-

standardagents/spec.description: Standard Agent Specification — an open-source standard for creating portable, composable, domain-specific agents.
standardagents/spec.readme:
Standard Agent Specification

An open standard for portable, composable, domain-specific agents.

Specification · Runtimes · Community

## About The Standard Agent Specification defines agents and the requirements for their runtimes. It covers agent components, execution, and packaging. Agents built with the specification can be published, installed, and composed with other Standard Agents. The specification is for people and coding agents building or reviewing agents, runtimes, and tools. This repository contains the specification text in `content/` and the Astro site that publishes it. The current specification version is 0.2.0. ## Documentation Read the [overview](https://standardagentspec.org/) for the principles and structure of the specification. The documentation includes [examples](https://standardagentspec.org/0.2.0/getting-started/examples), [agent definitions](https://standardagentspec.org/0.2.0/specification/agents), [runtime requirements](https://standardagentspec.org/0.2.0/infrastructure/runtime), and [packaging](https://standardagentspec.org/0.2.0/distribution/packaging). The [documentation index for coding agents](https://standardagentspec.org/llms.txt) links to the current specification pages. ## Runtimes A runtime executes Standard Agents. An agent package that follows the specification runs the same way in each runtime. | Runtime | Description | | --- | --- | | [Standard Agents Builder](https://standardagents.ai) | A runtime and builder interface from Standard Agents. It runs on Cloudflare Workers. | | Your runtime | The list is open to every runtime that implements the specification. [Submit yours](https://standardagentspec.org/runtimes#submit-a-runtime). | To add a runtime, open a pull request that adds it to `src/data/runtimes.md`. The [runtimes page](https://standardagentspec.org/runtimes#submit-a-runtime) lists what an entry needs. ## Contributing Propose a change through a GitHub [issue](https://github.com/standardagents/spec/issues) or [pull request](https://github.com/standardagents/spec/pulls).
